question: Are LAP and the comparator checks right when the true LAP is known?

design.data_and_split: as scripts/validate_instrument.py (same _cfg and seeds): 2,000 programs, 1,500 targets; train info_time <= 2016, test 2017-2020, target-disjoint
design.representations: deployable X(0); aggregate naive X(inf); separated naive X_sep = [X(0), X_post], X_post = the 14 evidence aggregates from evidence_date > info_time only
design.learner: models.fit_gbdt (HistGradientBoosting, depth 3, lr 0.06, 300 iter, l2 1.0, seed 0)
design.truth: AP_pop(naive fit) - AP_pop(deployable fit) on 66,000 fresh programs from the replicate's own stream (synth.generate with n_programs = 2,000 + 66,000, n_targets unchanged; first 2,000 programs asserted identical to the replicate, so area effects and leak settings match), restricted to info_time 2017-2020. target_effect_sd = 0, so target ids are independent of covariates, evidence and labels and the target-disjoint filter is a random thinning of the 2017-2020 programs. Truth sampling error from even/odd half-samples.
design.lap_ci: target-clustered paired percentile bootstrap, 200 resamples, seed = replicate
design.permutation: compare_methods.permutation, 20 permutations, seed 0, X_sep model, X_post columns; population joint PI from 3 permutations
design.univariate_screen: compare_methods.screen on the training block, flags >= 0.9 and >= 0.8
design.drop_and_refit: drop the X_post column with the largest single-column permutation drop, refit; residual = its population LAP; share = residual / true X_sep LAP
design.sensitivity: truth from one separate-seed population per level (66,000 programs, seed 990000 + 1,000 * level index), which has different area effects
design.mcse: sd / sqrt(R) for means; sqrt(p (1 - p) / R) for rates

drop_top_ranked_post_column.residual_share: undefined (true LAP is about 0 at level 0)
